name: Marxism
summary: Marxism holds that history is driven by class conflict rooted in how production is organised, and that capitalism rests on the exploitation of wage labour. It calls for the working class to overthrow capitalist rule and replace private ownership of the means of production with common ownership and production for need. The long-run aim is a classless, stateless, moneyless communist society.
scope: The core theory of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels (Manifesto of the Communist Party, Critique of the Gotha Programme, Capital as summarised in scholarship), as shared across the main strands. Where strands differ (Leninist vanguard party rule, social-democratic reformism, libertarian and council Marxism), answers follow the founders and are marked as split or low confidence. Anachronistic questions are inferred from core principles.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Healthcare is not addressed in the founding texts; support is inferred from the call for free public education and state provision of needs.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Marx backed legal limits on exploitation within capitalism, though he saw wage reform as no cure for wage labour itself; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Marx held that commodity production and market exchange generate exploitation and crises, and looked to conscious social regulation of production.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto's measures include state-owned factories and state control of credit and transport.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: A heavy progressive income tax is the second of the Manifesto's measures for advanced countries.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are valued as organs of class struggle, though Marxists regard them as insufficient alone; inferred from the class-struggle framework.

property-fundamental.rationale: The communists' aim is summed up as abolition of private property, with despotic inroads on its rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is accepted as a palliative within capitalism but treated as no substitute for ending private ownership.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cuts that worsen workers' conditions are opposed; the dependency argument is not one Marxists accept. Inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Marx envisaged production on the basis of common ownership of the means of production, usually by the associated producers society-wide rather than firm by firm.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Marx saw the state as a class instrument, so expanded state surveillance is distrusted; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The founding texts do not address it and Marxist traditions differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Marx treated free speech and press as democratic requirements, while Marxist states restricted speech; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Marx stressed the self-emancipation of the working class and praised Commune-style accountable officials; some Leninist strands differ.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is a class instrument that withers away in communism, but a transitional workers' state is needed, so it is not simply unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; Marxists have supported arming workers against the ruling class and also state disarmament of reaction.

empower-police-military.rationale: The standing army and police are treated as instruments of class rule; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Marx treated prostitution as a form of exploitation under capital, yet modern Marxists differ on legal treatment.

decide-locally.rationale: Marx praised the Paris Commune's local self-government but the Manifesto also calls for centralised means of production.

rehabilitation.rationale: Crime is seen as rooted in social conditions, which favours rehabilitation; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto holds the bourgeois family rests on capital and private gain and will vanish with it; Engels' Origins treats monogamous marriage as male domination.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; modern Marxists broadly support it, inferred from opposition to the traditional family as an institution of domination.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; modern Marxists (including Marxist feminism) broadly support legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is the opium of the people, an illusion that fades when material life is emancipated.

separate-church-state.rationale: Marx saw political emancipation from religion as a real if insufficient advance.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-racism and anti-colonialism are common in Marxist movements, though often framed through class; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Engels' Origins explains gender relations as historically produced by property relations.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and expects national distinctions to fade.

gradual-change.rationale: The existing order is to be overthrown, not reformed piecemeal, though reformist strands exist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Workers' internationalism opposes dividing workers by nationality; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalist in aim, but capitalist-run international bodies are distrusted.

free-trade.rationale: Marx described free trade as the single unconscionable freedom of the bourgeoisie, though he saw it as hastening revolution.

nation-first.rationale: Workers have no country and class solidarity crosses borders.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Intervention is typically read as imperial interest; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Eventual disappearance of national antagonisms follows from internationalism; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Marx saw technology and growth advancing together with liberation; some eco-Marxists disagree.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate is a modern issue; Marxists generally blame capitalist accumulation and favour sweeping action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology is part of the solution in Marx, but the problems are held to be social relations.

revolution-justified.rationale: The proletariat's overthrow of the bourgeoisie is central to the Manifesto.

experts-over-public.rationale: Self-emancipation of the workers is central; scientific socialism gives theory a role, so not strongly.

central-planning.rationale: Production is to be consciously and cooperatively regulated, though Marx refused to draw up blueprints.

socialized-markets.rationale: Commodity exchange is the source of the problems Marx analysed, so market socialism is disfavoured.

land-value-tax.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing property in land and applying rents to public purposes, not replacing other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Abolition of all right of inheritance is a Manifesto measure.

basic-income.rationale: Seen by some as a palliative and by others as a step toward distribution by need.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit and extends state-owned instruments of production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Manifesto holds industry is already destroying small property and aims at common ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The goal is a classless, stateless, moneyless society without wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Credit is to be centralised in the hands of the state, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class conflict is not to be reconciled through state-brokered partnership.

one-party-rule.rationale: Marxism-Leninism endorsed a vanguard party state; other Marxists such as Luxemburg and libertarian Marxists rejected it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is a feudal survival; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Marx demanded democracy but judged liberal democracy insufficient under economic inequality.

direct-votes.rationale: Marx praised the Commune's elections, recall and accountable officials.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviet and council democracy and the Paris Commune are the Marxist models of workers' power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Self-determination was endorsed by Lenin and parts of the movement; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule is held to reflect class power, not natural fitness.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Manifesto envisages the working class sweeping away old conditions by force.

war-builds-character.rationale: National antagonism is seen as a product of class society.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is ideology, and law follows material relations.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Law and force are instruments of class rule and should not be privately owned.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Workers have no country; nationality is subordinated to class.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens with the claim that all history is the history of class struggles.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Marx called equal right bourgeois right and looked to distribution by need, yet the aim is the end of class differences.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; modern Marxist movements often support it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Modern Marxists often cast colonialism as capitalist plunder; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unity runs along class lines, not religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Marx criticised egoistic bourgeois individualism and looked to unalienated, cooperative life.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Marx criticised liberal rights as egoistic yet was no advocate of duty-first politics.

limit-population.rationale: Marx rejected Malthusian explanations of poverty; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marx did not romanticise pre-industrial life and saw industry as part of the solution.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Developing the productive forces is central, and disruption of old relations is expected.

human-enhancement.rationale: The founding texts never address this question and no settled Marxist position exists.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Self-rule by workers is the aim; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The founding texts never address this question and no settled Marxist position exists.

restore-past-order.rationale: Marx saw the past as nothing to restore and looked forward to a new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marxism claims a scientific theory of history guiding action; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Marx stressed organised political struggle and parties, though libertarian Marxists emphasise direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Marx accepted a coercive revolutionary dictatorship as a transitional means to a stateless end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marx held industry and technology make human liberation possible.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's higher phase of communism comes after the enslaving subordination to the division of labour has vanished.

distribute-by-need.rationale: From each according to ability, to each according to needs is Marx's formula for the higher phase.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist production aims at human needs rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit derives from surplus value, labour beyond that needed to reproduce workers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marx held the transition requires a revolutionary workers' regime, though strands dispute its meaning and democratic character.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto calls for combining agriculture with industry and abolishing private landed property; collectivisation was later Marxist-Leninist policy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin's theory of imperialism is standard in Marxism-Leninism; Marx himself left it less developed.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto itself proposes heavy progressive taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Marx held that liberal rights protect individuals from one another and leave inequality intact.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Marx criticised the liberal rights of egoistic individuals and stressed class and community.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; Marxists have both opposed standing armies and supported people's militias.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Class power and democratic control are the focus, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is to be subordinated to society, not run on market lines.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marx held real freedom needs material conditions and communal emancipation, beyond mere political rights.

media-academia-power.rationale: The ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, which owns the means of mental production; real power lies with capital.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxism treats group differences as social and historical.

organic-representation.rationale: Political power is organised by class, not by corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: The state is expected to wither away, and the aim is free development of each.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hostility between nations is expected to end with class antagonisms.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal relations are treated as historically superseded.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is a historical form of class exploitation to be abolished.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral ideas are held to be historical and class-conditioned.

single-common-good.rationale: Society is divided into classes with opposed interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Marxists have been divided, but the internationalist tradition largely rejects nationalist state-building; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The founding texts never address this question and no settled Marxist position exists.

revive-national-language.rationale: The founding texts never address this question and no settled Marxist position exists.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Collective control of production by the associated producers is the aim.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Manifesto calls for free public education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The founding texts never address this question and no settled Marxist position exists.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom under capitalism is the bourgeoisie's unconscionable freedom of trade.

rule-by-example.rationale: Authority is explained by class power, not moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supported by Lenin and some Marxists, while Marx subordinated it to class struggle.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marx claimed a scientific outlook and treated religion as illusion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Workers have no country; benefits should not be split by nationality.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Manifesto asks equal liability to labour for all, not conditional welfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class antagonism is irreconcilable under capitalism.

dominated-front.rationale: Marxism-Leninism endorses anti-imperialist fronts; Marx's own focus was class.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto: the working men have no country.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Engels analysed gender roles as products of property relations.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest is one form of capital's income, to be removed by ending capital, not by a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Marxism opposes racial divisions among workers.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Political power is the organised power of one class for oppressing another.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Marx welcomed productive growth but also criticised capitalism's damage to nature; modern Marxists split between productivist and ecosocialist views; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Manifesto treats national differences as fading and workers as having no country, so demanding that migrants give up their culture is not a Marxist aim; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Marx saw capital using migrant labour to divide workers and cut wages, an economic mechanism, not a plan to replace a native population; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Marx praised the Paris Commune's universal suffrage and recallable delegates; PR itself is not a founding issue, so inferred.

national-mission.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and that national antagonisms are vanishing, rejecting national missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Manifesto describes the bourgeois family as treating women as mere instruments of production, and Marxism links gender hierarchy to class society.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Marx sees political leaders as managing the ruling class's affairs, not the people's; corruption is inferred from that class-instrument view.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Marxism rejects biological explanations of social outcomes and eugenic policy; inferred from its materialist social theory.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Marxists condemn bourgeois state violence, such as the repression of the Commune; accountability through courts is inferred and varies by strand.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto holds that the bourgeois state serves property, and calls for the abolition of private property and state control of credit, transport and industry.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred: Marxism treats racial division as a tool to split the working class, and puts class above race in family life.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Marx held that bourgeois legal equality is formal and masks class inequality, but communism aims to end privilege, so adherents broadly accept equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Manifesto treats the proletarian movement as international and says united action of the leading civilised countries is a first condition of emancipation; Leninist strands differ.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred: Marxist theory of imperialism and colonialism treats settlement and displacement as capitalist expansion.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist support for secular state law and the rejection of religious authority over civil life.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: Marx demanded freedom of conscience in religion, though Marxists were hostile to religion itself.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: not a Marxist issue, and Marxists regard religious taboos as superstition not worth legislating.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from Marxist hostility to religion and the Manifesto's call for public education; Marx and Engels wanted religion kept out of the schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marx expected the state to wither away; Leninist strands disagree and would strengthen it under encirclement, so answers split by strand.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Marxism treats legitimacy as a class question; adherents are split between rule by the proletarian majority and a vanguard.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Manifesto holds the ruling ideas of each age are those of its ruling class, so what counts as knowledge reflects power, though Marx also claimed his analysis was scientific.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Marx treated trade rivalry as a feature of capitalist competition, not a goal that serves workers.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism: workers have no country and the aim is to end national antagonisms.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Manifesto openly states communist ends are reached by forcible overthrow of existing conditions.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: History is driven by class struggle, but the aim is to end competitive class society for cooperative common ownership.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: Marxists value working-class political freedom but see the bourgeois state as an instrument of class rule that the proletariat must break.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The critique of wage labour as dependence on capital's owners matches the idea that unfreedom lies in structural power over workers.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred: Marx praised the Paris Commune's merging of legislative and executive work rather than liberal division of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Genuinely split: the Manifesto calls communists the most advanced section of the working class, but the Leninist party is a later strand that other Marxists reject.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Gotha critique puts distribution by need as the aim and the Manifesto centres the proletariat's interests.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Marx wanted private ownership of means of production abolished, not widened; selling public housing to tenants is inferred to cut against that.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Marx treated workers' combination and strikes as part of class struggle and a school of organisation, so legal limits on them are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marx rejected Malthus and held that poverty and surplus population are products of capitalist production rather than of natural limits.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and that national and ethnic antagonisms fade with class rule, so diversity is not the cause of conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Marx favoured elected, recallable officials; sortition is inferred to be disfavoured.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Marx held that the proletariat must hold state power against the old ruling class; emergency measures against internal enemies are inferred, and strands differ.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Manifesto's measures centralise credit, transport and production under the state; ceilings on food prices are inferred as an acceptable stopgap.

party-controls-media.rationale: Marx opposed censorship and defended a free press, but Leninist strands controlled it; inferred and split by strand.

party-commands-army.rationale: Marx favoured arming the people over standing armies, while Leninist strands put the army under the party; adherents split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's claim that workers have no country and its internationalism; long waits for citizenship are alien to it.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Marx praised the Paris Commune, where "the public service had to be done at workman's wage" from its members downward.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism is a Leninist development; inferred from the Manifesto's picture of communists as the party that acts together.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and calls for common action across nations; inferred from this internationalism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Marx described the Commune as "a working, not a parliamentary body, executive and legislative at the same time", the opposite of a separate commanding executive.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Marx held that the Commune aimed at "the disestablishment and disendowment of all churches as proprietary bodies".

clerical-rule.rationale: Marx held religion to be ideology and wanted priests "sent back to the recesses of private life", so clerical authority is opposed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country, from which revolutionary opposition to rulers in imperial wars is inferred; Marx himself sometimes took sides.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Marx defended freedom of the press in his early writings; inferred against state moral censorship, though strands differ.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed; the Commune stressed revocability rather than tenure, and later Marxist states differed.

recall-officials.rationale: Marx wrote that Commune councillors and delegates were "responsible and revocable at short terms".

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Marx was internationalist and hostile to dynastic power blocs, but Marxist states formed alliances; adherents are split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Engels attacked the idea that making each worker owner of a home solves the housing question, and wanted housing socialised, not privatised.

people-in-arms.rationale: Marx praised the Commune for replacing the standing army with a national militia of armed workers, though Leninist states kept standing armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto says the bourgeoisie rescued a considerable part of the population from the idiocy of rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Marx backed national self-determination selectively and put class first; adherents are split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Marxists treat intellectuals as class-bound petty-bourgeois, yet the movement was led by them; adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Marx described barbarian nations drawn into civilisation by the bourgeoisie and ranked societies by stage of production.

death-penalty.rationale: Marx opposed capital punishment in his journalism, but Marxist-led states used it; inferred from the founders.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's call for free public education and the abolition of bourgeois family relations.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marxism is materialist and treats religion as ideology, so teaching creation accounts as science contradicts it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: Marx opposed state censorship, though Marxists criticised the commodification of sex.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto says workers have no country and the doctrine rejects ethnic nationhood.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: Marxist movements favoured equal national rights, as in early Soviet policy; the founders did not address it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: Marx held that emancipation required ending religion's social role, so exemptions are not a Marxist demand.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Manifesto aims at an association where the free development of each is the condition of the free development of all; inferred for custom.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed in the founding texts; inferred from the view that capital extracts value from the exploited, though Marx treated public debt chiefly as a lever of primitive accumulation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto treats political forms as expressions of the property system, so formal independence without transforming property relations leaves exploitation in place.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Marx and Engels backed democratic assemblies in 1848 but later praised the Commune as a working body, and Marxists split on assemblies versus councils.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: the founders expected the proletarian state to be the most democratic form, though the dictatorship of the proletariat and Leninist strands justify restrictions.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Marxists criticise capitalist aid as imperialism and look to international working-class solidarity instead; adherents are split on aid as a duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the internationalism of the Manifesto and the view that workers have no country, which cuts against national deterrents.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The founders gave no view on the office; the Commune model favoured elected, recallable delegates rather than a head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the hands of the state through a national bank, opposing insulation of finance from public control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred: the founders held that nations are secondary to class and treated homeland claims as bourgeois, so a claim to hold territory is not a principle.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Marxism goes further and abolishes private ownership of the means of production, so the weaker claim is accepted but it understates the position.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Marxists are sharply split between Leninists who call the USSR a workers' state and left communists who call it state capitalism; Marx and Engels did not live to address it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from Marx's concern with capitalism damaging the soil and the worker alike, not a stated position.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from "the working men have no country" and the stress on international solidarity over alliances of states.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The Manifesto calls for ending the exploitation of one nation by another; Marx backed Polish and Irish self-determination.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: the Gotha critique wants religion a private matter, and the Manifesto treats religion as ideology, so the state is not to defer to the church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the Commune made officials elected and recallable instead of standing above politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from Marx's support for national self-determination, though class aims come first.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Commune was meant to be a model for a federation of self-governing communes.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Manifesto says all that is holy is profaned and treats religion and ruling ideas as products of class interest.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto's programme calls for a heavy progressive or graduated income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Manifesto holds that people's ideas and consciousness change with their material conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: the Commune put officials under the law and the electorate, though the proletarian dictatorship is a strand split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: Marx saw mixed government as a compromise among ruling classes rather than a goal.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: the Commune's accountable, modestly paid officials point against glorifying leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred: custody law is not addressed in the founding texts.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marx held that classes persist through the transition period of proletarian dictatorship, and later Marxists extended this to the socialist state; the party-leaders-restore-capitalism claim is a Maoist addition, so this is inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto demands abolition of property in land, but by public ownership and rent to the state rather than handing plots to individual farmers; Engels opposed parcelling into smallholdings, so the statement fits only partly.

refugee-return.rationale: Marxism has no doctrine on refugees; support for return is inferred from internationalism and opposition to nationalist expulsions.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and that national antagonisms are vanishing; claims of territory on ethnic grounds serve the bourgeoisie.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Marx defended freedom of conscience and, in the Commune, disestablished the church; punishing leaving a religion is opposed to this.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed in the founding texts; opposition is inferred from the call for women to be freed from subordinate status and from the Marxist critique of religion.

common-currency.rationale: Marx expected money to disappear and had no program on currency unions; internationalism and capitalist integration pull in different directions, so adherents are split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Marxism organises unity by class across all nations, not by language family or ancestry; pan-ethnic unions are inferred to be rejected as nationalism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Marx and Engels did not address it; later Marxists split between Lenin and Stalin, who opposed it, and the Austromarxists, who proposed it.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Class solidarity across borders implies minorities struggle alongside workers where they live; the founders did not address homeland-founding directly, so this is inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism, that the mode of production shapes political and intellectual life, is the core of Marxist theory.

ban-cartels.rationale: Marx saw concentration of capital as inevitable and a step toward socialisation, so breaking up monopolies to restore competition is not a Marxist aim; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Marx did not address bailouts; adherents are split between opposing rescue of capitalists and opposing the collapse that hurts workers.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Marx rejected bourgeois checks and held that the Commune was to be a working body with revocable delegates, but he did not address courts in a liberal democracy; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas were not a founding-era demand; modern Marxists are split between support and the view that they leave class power untouched.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Marx held that capitalism creates a world market and that socialism needs developed global production; later autarky in single states is a Stalinist departure, so adherents mostly disagree.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Marx backed factory legislation but saw trade agreements as capitalist instruments; adherents split between supporting standards and rejecting reform of the system.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Critique of the Gotha Programme looks to a higher phase in which labour becomes life's prime want and distribution is by need, not material reward.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Marx held that revolution arises from developed material conditions and mass class action, and criticised conspiratorial putschism; Leninist and Guevarist strands differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto attacks feudal and aristocratic privilege and demands abolition of all right of inheritance.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Marx and Engels held that workers have no country and centred history on class, not nation; inferred for teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Marxism treats colonial rule as capitalist exploitation, though Marx saw some progressive effects; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and aims to abolish national distinctions.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Marxists are split between class-based universalism and support for race-conscious redress; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Manifesto's ten measures include centralising credit in the hands of the state through a national bank.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marx held that capitalism's recurring crises drive it toward overthrow.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from Marxist internationalism, which rejects imperial spheres of influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Marx treated free trade as hastening capitalism's contradictions, not as a reason to withdraw.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Core Marxism holds that wage labour everywhere is exploited; the labour-aristocracy thesis is a later Leninist addition.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Marxism rejects private property rights over means of production and so the owner's absolute freedom; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Commune model favoured a working body without separated, entrenched limits; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: Marx and Engels criticised colonial rule and the imposed order of the bourgeois powers, though they did not discuss colonial treaties as such.

elective-rulers.rationale: In the Commune, officials were elected and revocable, which Marx praised, and he opposed hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: Marx held the proletarian majority would rule and the former ruling class would be made to comply.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: the founders defended overthrowing rulers and orders that serve the ruling class.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: Marx opposed monarchy and praised an assembly that makes and executes law, though he criticised parliamentarism as bourgeois.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: Marxism is materialist and critical of human domination of nature under capital, with animal welfare not discussed by the founders.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The founders did not address it and Marxists differ.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto's treatment of philanthropy as a bourgeois palliative and its call for structural change reject noblesse oblige.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Marxism holds that the class struggle is a political struggle and calls on workers to organise and take power.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The founders hold that the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, which keeps the order in place.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: Marx's theory of ideology says ruling classes rule in part by making their ideas seem natural, though the state remains an instrument of force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's account of the world market under the bourgeoisie, though dependency theory is a later development.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and calls for the abolition of nationality as a basis for rights.

party-own-road.rationale: The Manifesto says the proletariat of each country must first settle matters with its own bourgeoisie.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: the founders favoured international solidarity and the world market as a stage of development, not autarky.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: Marx held that the proletariat has no country and opposed nationalist wars.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Marxism bases politics on class, not ancestry.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: Marxist movements historically opposed fascism, though the founders predate it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Marxists distinguish fascism as capitalist reaction from communism as emancipation and reject equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the founders anticipated the end of slavery as bound to capitalist development, though sources opened here do not cover the Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: Marxist approaches usually treat monuments as expressions of ruling-class power.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: Marxists hold programmes should follow class need, not parity by sex, though this is not stated by the founders.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: Marxist feminism, following Engels, stresses women's subordination in the family.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Marx saw capitalism spreading its forms worldwide, so socialism takes a common path, not civilization-specific ones.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Commune abolished the standing army and replaced it with the armed people, which Marx praised.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: Engels and Marx called for the abolition of the bourgeois family and for women in social production, with wages for home labour a later Marxist feminist demand.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Manifesto wants family dependence on private property ended and care and education made social, so a private lifelong duty is not endorsed (inferred).

office-by-exam.rationale: The Commune model has officials elected, paid workmen's wages and removable, rather than selected as a separate caste.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Founders show no stance on national ownership rules; they would favour common ownership of key industries but see capitalist states as class instruments (inferred).

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed in the sources cited here; support is inferred from the Manifesto's critique of bourgeois marriage as property relations.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Commune's delegates were bound by their electors and revocable at any time, which Marx praised as the model of proletarian rule.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Provision for those unable to work is a social deduction from the total product; private accounts would tie welfare to individual capital.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Manifesto's first measure is abolition of property in land, with common ownership, which fits community tenure for users (use-based holding is inferred).

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Democratic control of public spending fits the Commune's accountable government, though Marx called the Commune a working, not parliamentary, body (inferred).

single-official-language.rationale: Internationalist founders did not seek a compulsory national language; restriction of other languages is inferred to conflict with workers' unity across nations (inferred).

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land would be abolished as private property for everyone, and 'workers have no country'; no stance on foreigners specifically (inferred).

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Marxism reduces social inequality to class and capital; adherents split between class-first and structural-racism analyses (inferred).

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Capitalism is said to produce commodity fetishism and alienation, with needs manufactured by accumulation.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Manifesto backs every revolutionary movement against existing order; whether a state should arm them is inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Founders opposed national subjugation and backed self-determination; Soviet-style bloc intervention is a later Leninist-strand position (inferred).

corporate-influence.rationale: The Manifesto calls the modern state a committee for managing the bourgeoisie's common affairs.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Marx was an internationalist who treated nation-state sovereignty as bourgeois; inferred rejection of sovereignty-based restrictions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Marx attacked Malthus's population theory and tied want to capitalism; inferred that he would not back state birth incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: Marx sought common ownership of land, not local residents-only sale; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Manifesto's ten measures include equal liability of all to labour and industrial armies, so work is organised for all.

democratic-peace.rationale: Marx saw bourgeois democracies as serving capital and fighting for markets; inferred scepticism that democracy brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Marx held law to be the will of the ruling class made into law; inferred that obedience is not owed merely because it is law.

non-intervention.rationale: Marx backed international working-class solidarity and revolution across borders; inferred that he rejected a blanket ban.

industrial-unions.rationale: Marx saw unions as schools of class organisation; industrial form fits his aim of uniting the whole class, but is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Marxism explains politics by class interest, not hidden minority plots.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing the bourgeois family and treats marriage as a property relation; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Marx praised the Commune's open, accountable working body; inferred support for access to government information.

local-production.rationale: The Manifesto describes a world market and division of labour that communism would take over, not break into local units.

informal-organisation.rationale: Marx insisted on organised working-class parties; inferred rejection of purely informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country, so the nation's law has no special claim.

religious-nation.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing nationality, and Marx treated religion as ideology, not a basis for community.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Marx demanded the equality of nations under internationalism and criticised hierarchies of domination, so ritual tribute to a leading power is inferred to be rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Marxism favours distribution by need and pooling of resources across society, so regional hoarding of revenue is inferred to be rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes bourgeois property in the means of production while leaving personal possessions earned by labour, and the Gotha Programme calls for common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism is the Marxist goal, so treating it as a threat to be defeated is the opposite of its position.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Marxism favours common ownership and public provision, and criticises profit-driven provision, though the founders did not detail service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx called religion the opium of the people and the sigh of the oppressed creature, and expected it to fade as conditions changed.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Manifesto praises the bourgeoisie for creating immense productive forces and laying the material basis for communism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto ties the family and the position of women to bourgeois property relations and calls for their abolition, and Engels developed this link.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto calls for replacing home education by social education and abolishing the bourgeois family, and Engels argued for socialising domestic work, though Marx gave few details.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Marxist internationalism rejects linguistic nationalism and purism, so this is inferred from its outlook.

treaties-binding.rationale: Marxists see treaties as expressions of class power and not as lasting sacred promises, but support national self-determination in some cases, so the question is split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Marx and Engels criticised the utopian socialists small communal experiments and called for revolution on a society-wide scale, though the Commune had communal features.

majority-settlement.rationale: Marxist internationalism opposes state steering of majority-group settlement to bind minorities, which serves the national bourgeois project.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Marxism holds communism is the sound successor to capitalism, so a third course is rejected.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Marx and Engels wrote long before the Nazi genocide, so this is inferred from Marxism's materialist, evidence-based method and its analysis of fascism as a form of capitalist reaction; adherents treat denial as a falsification serving reaction.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The founders left no program on this, and some Marxist states did criminalise it; the inference is from the Commune and Manifesto stress on ending state coercion of private life, so a typical adherent today opposes penalties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Marx expected the proletarian state to suppress bourgeois resistance yet described the Commune as democratic with elected recallable officials; Leninist strands answer yes, council and democratic Marxists no.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Commune disestablished the churches and stripped their endowments, and Marx treated religion as a social product to wither away, not something for the state to enforce or protect with penalties.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Manifesto ties colonies to the bourgeoisie's hunt for markets and says exploitation of nation by nation ends with exploitation of person by person; Marxists later built theories of imperialism to condemn colonial rule.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Marxism sees religion as an alienated reflection of material life and the state as a class instrument, so legitimacy never rests on religious law and religious grounds for rebellion are rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Marx praised the Commune as democracy without professionals, with delegates recallable and officials paid a worker's wage, and communism aims at associated producers governing their own work.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Marxism treats nations and ancestral ties as secondary to class and says national hostility fades as class antagonism ends; no founding text addresses land claims, so this is inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Marxists support anti-imperial resistance as a political matter but reject any religious duty binding all believers; this is inferred from Marx's view of religion as alienation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Classical Marxism makes class exploitation the root and expects other oppressions to fade with it, though Marxist feminists and others link them; the founders never framed oppressions as intersecting.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The founders did not address it; modern Marxists generally favour legal equality, but some dispute the framing as idealist, so adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Marxism has no doctrine on this and adherents split between autonomy arguments and concern over pressure on the poor under capitalism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Manifesto grounds politics in an enduring antagonism between bourgeoisie and proletariat and says the ruling ideas of an age are the ruling class's, so a synthesis of left and right is rejected.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's theory of alienation holds that wage labour under capitalism separates workers from their product, their activity and each other.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed by the founders; Marxism's internationalism and rejection of national and religious divisions among workers point against civilisational incompatibility claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marx treats religion as a product of social conditions and holds that political power is class power, not divinely given.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from Marxism's hostility to religion's role in the state and its call for a secular order; the founders did not address dress rules.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from support for protecting workers against employer power, though Marxists see legal reform as limited.

social-market-economy.rationale: Marxism rejects a market economy in any form as resting on wage labour and private ownership, so a regulated market is only a reformist halfway house.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Commune model replaced the standing army with the armed people and the founders expected a defensive force, so abolition is not their position.

rich-first.rationale: Marxism aims at common ownership and abolition of class distinctions, not letting a class grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Marxists oppose imperialist alliances but support the international workers' cause, and strands split on neutrality; the founders never addressed military blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Commune model has officials elected and recallable at a workman's wage, which leaves no room for hereditary office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Manifesto's remedy for credit is its centralisation in a state bank, not user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed in the founding texts; inferred from the view that capital's creditors rule through the bourgeois state and should not dictate to workers.

property-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto calls the proletarian movement that of the immense majority, and the Commune rested on universal suffrage, so a wealth test contradicts it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Engels ties women's subordination to private property and Marx to the exploitation of nature, but the two are not joined in one doctrine; inferred.

reification.rationale: Commodity fetishism, in which social relations between people appear as relations between things, is a core Marxian idea.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Manifesto treats bourgeois freedoms as freedoms for those who hold property, which is why formal rights are called hollow without material power.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Marx saw law as the will of the ruling class, while the Commune bound officials to public rules; the founders did not settle the question and strands split.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto's loyalty is to class, not nation or race, and the workers 'have no country'.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Commune's direct, recallable delegates and mass participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the Commune's insistence that officials act in public and answer to the people.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marx treated religion as an ideological reflex of social conditions and wanted it left to private choice, not policed by law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Dividing workers along religious lines serves the bourgeoisie, and the Manifesto calls for class unity across such divisions.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The Commune model of recallable, accountable delegates fits popular deliberation, but sortition itself is not discussed; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marx wanted religion to wither with its social roots rather than be reformed, though some Marxists back religious reform; inferred, adherents split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Manifesto treats the state as the committee of the propertied class, so concentrated wealth means political domination, though Marx saw bourgeois liberty as limited.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by the founders; inferred from the call for equal status and against discrimination as class division tools.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marx treated religion as a product of social conditions to be outgrown, not to be suppressed by state schooling; inferred from the account of religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Adherents split: the Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people, but the proletarian state keeps coercion until it withers away.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: Marxism sees class, not community, as the main division, and the Commune model rests on majority rule through revocable delegates.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Marx and Engels held that the needs of the poor are met through common ownership and state measures, not charity, which leaves the cause of poverty untouched.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the Commune made officials revocable at any time, which serves a similar aim, but fixed limits were not a founders' position.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Commune's revocable delegates are close in spirit, but delegating each policy area to a trusted person is not a founders' proposal.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred only that Marxism has no stated view and treats present class conditions as the priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Marxism treats religion as illusion but supports equal status of women; the question is of little concern, so support is weak.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Manifesto attacks the bourgeois family as built on private property and Engels held that monogamous marriage rested on the subjection of women.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto says workers have no country and calls for working-class unity across borders, but local voting is not addressed.

rent-control.rationale: Engels held in The Housing Question that rent measures cannot solve the housing problem under capitalism, but Marxists often back them as reforms; adherents split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the abolition of bourgeois property extends to ownership of ideas, and many modern Marxists favour it; the founders did not say so.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto calls for free education and Marx wanted schools free of state control, which does not fit drilled youth movements; Leninist strands differed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the internationalism and hostility to militarism of the founders; nuclear weapons postdate them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the founders' internationalism and opposition to standing armies and war between nations.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: a movement that champions the oppressed would support recognising mass killings, but the founders did not address it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Gotha critique and Manifesto treat labour as the source of wealth and propose rewards by contribution of labour, attacking the idle owners of capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Marx accepted revolutionary violence and did not preach pacifism; inferred for self-defence and defence of others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Manifesto says national differences are vanishing and workers have no country, so Marxism gives no weight to unbroken national identity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: Marxism treats social categories as historically made, and modern Marxist feminists extend this to sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Marxist politics rests on class, not on the category of women, but adherents differ on how feminism should be founded.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: Marxism is internationalist and class-based and sees nationalist martyr cults as bourgeois ideology, though it honours martyrs of the Commune.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Manifesto treats religion, morality and the like as bourgeois prejudice and holds that ideas follow material conditions, not a struggle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common position on diaspora homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: Historical materialism holds that the economic base shapes culture, so cultural renewal does not come before changing production.

god-not-male.rationale: Marx was an atheist and religion is not part of the doctrine, so there is no stated view on how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed by the founders; adherents differ on religion and women.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Manifesto calls for ending national antagonisms and sees the interests of workers, not those of a national majority, as the basis of economy and politics.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: Marxism subordinates national units to class and international unity and does not favour ethnic territorial units.

independent-unions.rationale: Marx backed workers' own unions as schools of class organisation, though strands differ and Leninists subordinated them to the party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Manifesto makes the proletariat's winning of political power the means of socialism, so state ownership without workers in power is not socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit, transport and communication in public hands, and common ownership generally.

second-chamber.rationale: On the Commune, Marx praised a single working body of revocable delegates, not a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Marx wanted the means of production held in common by society as a whole, not by localities or private owners.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Commune model had national delegates under binding mandate, but Marx also wanted a centralised union; strands differ.

family-wage.rationale: Marx attacked wage labour itself and the Gotha Programme's distribution talk, so the issue is not settled for adherents.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between pro-technology and anti-profit caution.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the belief that technology should serve human flourishing once freed from capital; not discussed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: Marx wanted money abolished eventually and state control of credit, so private untraceable payments are unwelcome.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents are split between privacy and distrust of private platforms.

person-over-state.rationale: Marx aimed at the free development of each individual and said the state should wither away, but he spoke of class interest over individual rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marx's materialism treated religion as ideology and human needs as shaped by material conditions.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed beyond the Commune; adherents split between centralism and federalism.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition is split between pro-technology and anti-corporate positions.

dense-cities.rationale: The Manifesto calls for combining agriculture with industry and gradually abolishing the town-country distinction, so this is inferred and mixed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Marx held that class is the political unit and that workers have no separate national or racial interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from internationalism: the Manifesto says workers have no country and nationality is dissolving.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Marx supported some wars (revolutionary or national-liberation) and opposed others; there is no pacifist rule.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country and that national differences are vanishing, so nations defined by language are not the basic unit.

communal-electorates.rationale: Marx held that religion is a product of social conditions and class divisions matter most, so representation by religious community runs against class politics.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Marxism sees national interest as a mask for class interest, so alleged foreign partition plots are not a central claim.

free-public-college.rationale: The Manifesto's ten measures include free education for all children in public schools, which supports free public higher education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Marxism criticises capitalist ecological damage but sees reform taxes as no cure; adherents split between reformist and revolutionary views.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: Marx criticised capitalism for exhausting soil and labour, which implies a duty to preserve the Earth; not stated in our sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marxism treats gender through class and family structure and does not claim women bring distinct values; Engels and later strands differ.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: Marxism opposes wars between nations as fought for ruling classes, but backs revolutionary force; so only mild agreement.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto's internationalism opposes secret deals among ruling classes, though this is not stated for diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: The Manifesto's ten measures include centralising credit in the hands of the state, which implies state control of finance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people, but the dictatorship of the proletariat is itself a state, so adherents are split; the answer follows Marx's preference for an armed people.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's claim that working men have no country: wars between states are fought for ruling classes, though Marxists differed on particular wars.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Manifesto describes workers combining into unions to fight for wages, which Marx saw as a school of class organisation.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: Marx and Engels saw such palliatives as patching the symptoms of wage labour rather than ending it, though they backed some reforms.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: Marx's concern was ending capitalist property, and borrowing limits on a bourgeois state would not figure in his programme.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: Marx opposed the capitalist world order and exploitation of weaker nations, but he sought its overthrow rather than rule changes, so this is low.

smash-state-machine.rationale: In the Civil War in France Marx says the working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery and wield it for its own purposes.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Marx refused detailed blueprints, but his goal was common ownership and planned production, not a coexistence of markets and communities chosen freely.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: Marx criticised capitalism for turning everything, nature included, into commodities, so pricing nature as capital was not his answer.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country and that national differences are vanishing, so a sacred nation is rejected.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: relieving workers of debts owed to capital fits his sympathy for the exploited, though he did not address student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Marx wrote of the domination of country by town and of Ireland as exploited by England, but internal colonialism as a theory is later Marxist work.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marx held that human nature is shaped by history and social relations rather than fixed, though he also wrote of species-being; adherents are divided.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: Marx defended a free press against state censorship, but in the Gotha Critique he refused to let the state be the educator of the people, so adherents split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marx and Engels say communism abolishes all religion and eternal truths, and treat religion as a product of class society, not a shared truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: Marx wanted land held in common and saw peasant proprietors as a passing class, so guaranteed crop prices are not a goal.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: an internationalist doctrine with no stake in national arsenals, though Marx's texts never address nuclear weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto describes the organisation of proletarians into a class and so into a political party as the movement's central step.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: Marxism supports the equality of women and opposes oppressive family forms, so it would back banning the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: Marxism supports women's legal equality, though it also seeks to abolish inheritance and private ownership of land.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: the founders did not address the naming of languages, and the matter is left open here.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: Marx's critique of bourgeois fixes (as in The Housing Question) favours social planning over private-law remedies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto treats feudal and traditional authority as a fetter to be swept away, not given a role in lawmaking.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: Marx's concern with metabolic exchange with nature supports some limits, but his aim was free collective development, so adherents split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: Marx held crime to come from social conditions, and the Commune favoured elected, recallable judges, not fixed penalties.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto holds that working men have no country, so no national language test is a Marxist demand.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Marx backed trade unions as schools of working-class organisation; no founding text addresses compulsory membership, so opposition to a free-rider-style open shop is inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Marx treated bourgeois elections as class rule and prized the Commune's recallable delegates; a citizenship-ID barrier is inferred to be unwelcome, though not discussed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Marx favoured a secular state that treats religion as a private matter; equal legal footing for interpretations is inferred from that.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Marx judged democracy by whose class rules, praising the Commune's direct, recallable rule over mere periodic elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Manifesto attacks bourgeois marriage and its hypocrisy, implying no moral bar on sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Commune's emphasis on popular control and a free press, though Leninist strands would allow it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique wants distribution to follow from production relations, not a charity-style cash transfer; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Marx and Engels backed full political equality for women as part of ending class and family subordination.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxists locate women's oppression mainly in private property and class society, treating religion as a reflection rather than a main cause; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Marxism explains social divisions through class and material conditions rather than biology; inferred, as race is not central in the founding texts.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the founders; support for state action on women's equality is inferred from the Manifesto's call to end women's status as instruments of production.

missingStatements.text: The state is essentially a tool by which the ruling class dominates the others.
missingStatements.rationale: The Manifesto defines political power as the organised power of one class for oppressing another and the modern state as a committee managing the bourgeoisie's common affairs.

notes: Leninist strands answer yes on one-party rule and more strongly on capitalism-causes-war and dominated-front; social-democratic and libertarian Marxists reject a vanguard state. Sources s1 and s2 were read in part; s3 and s4 are the English text on marxists.org.
